# Frontier Tuning opens to more customers, with new tools for your teams

[Ranveer Chandra](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/microsoft365dev/author/ranveerchandra)

Vice President

In June at Microsoft Build, we introduced Frontier Tuning and opened a private preview with a focused group of customers. The idea is to help AI work the way your business does, using your own expertise as the standard it’s measured against.

Since then, private preview customers have been building and testing tuned agents for work that matters to their business, and the product has grown with them. Today at Microsoft Ignite, we’re sharing three updates: new tools that let your own teams tune, a look at how EY is putting Frontier Tuning to work, and an expanded private preview so more organizations can get started.

[Sign up for the private preview](https://aka.ms/FrontierTuning)

### **Frontier Tuning expands private preview, putting tuning in the hands of your makers and experts.**

At launch, private preview customers worked closely with our Forward Deployed Engineers to define scenarios, set evaluation criteria and run tuning. What we learned from that work shaped the tools private preview customers can use starting today:

* **The Frontier Tuning plugin for GitHub Copilot** helps makers and subject-matter experts build a Tuning Environment together, drawing on how your work gets done through Work IQ.

* **The Frontier Tuning CLI and APIs** let developers run tuning from the tools they already use and build tuned skills into their own agents.

* **Publishing to Cowork as a plugin** puts your experts’ judgment in user’s hands once your makers sign off. And when users hit a case worth learning from, they can send it back to your Tuning Environment.

* **Model choice** , with GPT 6 Luna and MAI Code 2 Flash available for tuning in the private preview.

Your teams set the standard, run the work, and decide what moves to production.

Frontier Tuning opens to more customers, with new tools for your teams

Tuning is also coming to Microsoft Copilot Studio in the near future, so makers can evaluate and tune skills using a similar approach described here. We’ll share more as availability gets closer.

### **See the difference before it ships**

A Tuning Environment holds four things : task, rubrics that describe good work in your experts’ terms, samples for training and evaluation, and the tools your skill uses in production. That separation means you’re measuring how a tuned version handles cases it wasn’t trained on.

[Picture1 image](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/microsoft365dev/wp-content/uploads/sites/73/2026/11/Picture1-1.webp)

Tuning runs in rounds, a process called hill climbing. Each round produces a new version, grades it against your rubrics on the evaluation samples, and builds on what improves. Your makers review the results and choose which version, if any, goes to users. The Microsoft 365 Frontier Tuning service manages your samples, tools, rubrics and tuned models, with secure storage and access controls.

How far you climb depends on how rich your Tuning Environment is: rubrics that capture what good looks like to your experts, samples that reflect real cases, and the same tools and knowledge your skill uses in production.

You also choose what to tune. Many teams start by improving the skill itself, which keeps you flexible as you work across supported models. When you need more, model tuning brings your expertise into a model your organization manages.

### **Customer spotlight: EY**

Private preview customers are applying Frontier Tuning to specialized work where their own standards define quality.

For example, **EY** is tuning its Tax Advisor agent to help its tax professionals research more effectively, with EY’s professionals continuing to own the advice they give clients. EY’s tax experts encoded their methodology, voice and review standards as rubrics, and connected the Tuning Environment to the same precedent search the agent uses in production.

_“EY’s tax methodology and review standards are what make our advice trustworthy. Encoding them as rubrics let a small model learn to research, cite and hedge the way our professionals do, and on our own quality bar it now outperforms a frontier model.”_

**_Benjamin Ambrosino_** _, EY Global Tax Chief Technology Officer_

### **Keep improving after launch**

Work changes, and a tuned skill should keep up. Users in Cowork can choose to share examples from their own work back to your Tuning Environment. When requirements change or you want to try a different model, your team can refresh samples, update rubrics and run another round, using the same evaluation to compare the new version with the one in use today.

### **Join the expanded private preview**

We’re opening the private preview to more customers in the Frontier program. If you have specialized work, experts who know what good looks like, and a standard AI needs to meet before you’ll rely on it, we’d like to hear from you.

There’s no charge for Frontier Tuning during the private preview. Pricing details will be shared before it becomes more broadly available.

**Sign up for the private preview at** [**aka.ms/FrontierTuning**](https://aka.ms/frontiertuning)

By [Julie Koesmarno , view all posts by this author](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics-365/blog/author/julie-koesmarno/) , Principal Group Product Manager, Microsoft Dataverse and Business Applications in Work IQ.

[Read more about Dynamics 365 in Copilot and other Microsoft Ignite announcements in Jeff Teper’s blog](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics-365/blog/business-leader/2026/11/17/microsoft-ignite-2026-introducing-dynamics-365-in-copilot/)

* * *

Enterprise AI pays off when Copilot and agents complete business processes from start to finish and IT can trust them to do it. That takes more than access to data. Agents need to understand how your business runs, follow the processes your teams follow, and act only within the permissions you set.

[Give agents and people the business context to act with Work IQ](https://ignite.microsoft.com/en-US/sessions/BRK299?source=sessions)

Today we’re announcing the general availability of [Business Applications in Work IQ](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/features/work-iq) . Work IQ grounds Microsoft Copilot and agents in your productivity data and in business data from Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Microsoft Power Platform. Your teams can now use it in production in Copilot Chat, Agent Builder, and Copilot Studio. Developers can bring it into any agent through the Work IQ protocols (MCP server, API, and CLI).

## Business Applications in Work IQ in action

Customers and partners are already putting Business Applications in Work IQ to work.

**Delta Dental** is using Business Applications in Work IQ to build Project Greenlight, an agent that turns ideas into actionable solutions. Employees simply say, “I have an idea,” and the agent asks five questions, logs the use case in Dataverse, and automatically drafts the complete documentation package, from solution assessment to architecture design.

> “Business Applications in Work IQ is a game changer for us. It turns our business knowledge into reusable business skills that access across enterprise safely and securely. With the right business context and connected systems, we can get work done more easily. And I’m not a developer–if I can build this, anyone can.”
> 
> **Gregory Stirewalt, Senior Engineer at Delta Dental of California**
> 
> 

Partners are these capabilities to work in industry scenarios, too. [Velrada](https://velrada.com/agentifying-your-power-platform-start-where-youve-already-proven-value/) , a global Microsoft Cloud Solution Partner worked with Microsoft to demonstrate how they can support mining shift handovers: incoming crews ask Copilot for the risks, priorities, and open actions held in the site’s operational apps. [Learn more about how Velrada creates consistent shift handovers by surfacing critical operational context with Work IQ.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0qX4Pqb1cuY)

[Discover what customers are building with Business Apps in Work IQ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2I3u_pe7Eqs)

## Why Work IQ works

Business processes work like a relay, and work often stalls at the handoff. Work IQ gives people and agents the records, relationships and processes from your business apps, so information and decisions carry from one step to the next.

1. **Keep your data in place.** Copilot and agents use the business context in your Dynamics 365 and Power Platform apps without moving your data.
2. **Understand your business.** Work IQ generates a semantic model in Dataverse, from the views, forms and relationships already in your apps, so agents know what your data means from day one.
3. **Follow your processes.** Business skills capture how your teams work. Every agent that uses them works from the same definitions and steps.
4. **Act within your permissions.** Every action is governed. Copilot and agents propose changes, follow any required approvals and update records only within each user’s permissions. Turning on Work IQ doesn’t give any user or agent access they didn’t already have.

## What’s generally available today

This release includes the following Business Applications in Work IQ capabilities:

* Business context in Copilot Chat, Agent Builder, and Copilot Studio.
* Business skills and automatically generated semantic models.
* Business context for pro-dev scenarios: Work IQ MCP server, CLI, and Dataverse Ask API.
* Admin controls in the Microsoft 365 and Power Platform admin centers.

## Here’s what this release means for each role

**Business users** ask Copilot Chat questions such as “Which renewals need my attention this quarter?” Copilot answers across Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service, and Power Apps, and links every answer to its source record. In Agent Builder, they build their own agents by choosing which business apps each agent should know.

[Learn more about adding Dynamics 365 and Power Apps data as a knowledge source to an agent in Agent Builder.](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder-add-knowledge)

[Watch now: See it in Copilot Chat and Agent Builder](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IU6JaNLhrME)

**Makers** start with the semantic model Work IQ generates and refine it with business terms the system can’t infer. Business skills turn a process, such as renewal readiness, into steps every agent follows. In Copilot Studio, Work IQ comes with every new agent, so agents start with business context and can update records within each user’s permissions.

* [Explore semantic models](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/semantic-model-overview)
* [Learn more about business skills](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-business-skill-overview)
* [Explore Work IQ in Copilot Studio](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq)

[Watch now: Turn business expertise into business skills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XCaaL6la0J0)

**Developers** bring the same business context into their own agents and apps. The Work IQ MCP server and CLI connect GitHub Copilot and clients such as n8n, Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor to your semantic models and business skills. The Dataverse Ask API answers a plain-language question from a semantic model and returns the matching records, a short summary and source links, limited to what the caller can read.

# Microsoft 365 Copilot and AI Agent readiness and resiliency with SharePoint Content Governance

[Sesha_Mani's avatar](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/users/sesha_mani/85036)

[Sesha\_Mani](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/users/sesha_mani/85036)

Icon for Microsoft rank Microsoft

Nov 17, 2026

**In the AI era, governance isn't a barrier to innovation. It's what makes innovation possible at scale.**

Winning with Copilot and AI agents takes more than speed and scale. It requires **readiness to embrace AI and resilience to recover when things go wrong** . That's the power of AI-first governance: accelerating innovation, strengthening trust, and maximizing AI return on investment.

Today at Microsoft Ignite ’26, we're announcing exciting new content governance innovations to help organizations accelerate their [Frontier Transformation](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/03/09/introducing-the-first-frontier-suite-built-on-intelligence-trust/) with AI Agents, Autopilots, Agent 365, and Work IQ.

## Governance innovations for resilient AI at scale

As you unveil AI Agents in your organization, either just getting started or deploying at scale, content governance becomes even more important to get right. **SharePoint is the #1 content citation source in Microsoft 365 Copilot and AI Agents** . Let us look into SharePoint content governance innovations across two main themes - readiness and resiliency, along with foundational security and enterprise lifecycle scenarios.

**Readiness for AI at scale** addresses oversharing, content lifecycle and sprawl, the risks boards now see as the biggest obstacles to AI transformation. New agentic skills power new security and storage management capabilities to address them.

**Resilient AI** is all about business continuity, especially in the era where agents are integral part of the workforce. Organizations must be prepared for unforeseen situations such as an agent going rogue and accidentally deleting content.

With this backdrop, let us dive into innovations across the following pillars:

Readiness for Copilot and AI Agents at Scale

SharePoint Admin Agent - Enhancements

Govern agents' traffic to M365 resources

Enhancements in SharePoint oversharing controls

Resilient AI: Business continuity even when agents go off script

Rewind when agents go off script

Microsoft 365 Backup: Teams support

Entra Backup

Security and Compliance capabilities in SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams

Microsoft 365 Storage Management and Enterprise Lifecycle

## Readiness for Copilot and AI Agents at Scale

Readiness is about ensuring your content is permissioned rightfully, organized in manageable clusters, has lifecycle guardrails, and in parallel knowing agent traffic across your Microsoft 365 estate _before_ AI Agents use it.

We are bringing many innovations to Copilot native governance capabilities powered by SAM (SharePoint Advanced Management) and to agent governance in the lens of Microsoft 365 resources. Let’s dive in.

#### 1\. SharePoint Admin Agent – Generally Available

At [Microsoft 365 Confernece’26](https://www.m365conf.com/) , we introduced the [SharePoint Admin Agent](https://aka.ms/M365-governance-agent) , Microsoft’s first-party AI assistant for managing your rapidly growing digital estate across Microsoft 365.

As the content backbone of Microsoft 365, SharePoint powers Teams, OneDrive, Loop, Copilot, and more. It sits at the center of content governance, spanning permissions, lifecycle, resilience, and relevance across users, apps, and now, AI agents.

The SharePoint Admin Agent brings these capabilities together in one simple conversational experience, with powerful skills across Permissions and Oversharing Management, Storage, Lifecycle, Multi-Geo, and Catalog. Today we are thrilled to announce many enhancements in the admin agent.

SharePoint Admin Agent skills

#### SharePoint Admin Agent’s Starter Prompts:

You can try various starter prompts categorized under various skills: Catalog, Permissions, Lifecycle, Storage, Organizational Settings and Multi-Geo.

#### Permissions and Oversharing Management skill – Generally Available

Admins can detect oversharing, see who has access to what and protect sensitive content, all in plain language. Ask _"Find overshared sites in my tenant"_ and the agent builds a prioritized list to review and act on, whether you have hundreds of sites or millions.

_SharePoint admin sees the permissions and oversharing skills of the SharePoint Management Agent in action._

#### Lifecycle skill – Generally Available

Ensuring content is current is critical to ensuring that Copilot serves the right content and with optimal utilization of storage. Helps admins stay in control of content from creation to end of life by identifying inactive, outdated, and ownerless sites and enabling actions like reviews and archival. For example, you could simply ask the agent: “ _List my inactive and ownerless sites_ ”.

_SharePoint admin sees the lifecycle skill of the SharePoint Management Agent in action._

#### Storage skill – Generally Available

Gives admins a clear view of tenant storage trends and active-versus-archive growth, helping them identify content sprawl, optimize capacity, and reduce unnecessary costs with confidence.

Here are some of the prompts that you can use in this v2 release, more enhancements are upcoming.

_"Compare active and archive SharePoint storage growth"_

_"Help me set up a file archive policy"_

_"How much version storage is used across the tenant?"_

_SharePoint admin sees the storage skill of the SharePoint Management Agent in action._

#### Multi-Geo skill – Generally Available

[Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo](https://aka.ms/M365MultiGeo) enables customers to comply with their organization's data residency requirements by ensuring that users' data is hosted within a specific geo where the user is located. The new **Multi-Geo skill in SharePoint Admin agent** assists the admin in moving the OneDrives to the user’s Preferred Data Location (PDL) along with following key capabilities:

* **Identify content to be moved**
* **Initiate moves:** Move OneDrive to users' Preferred Data Locations.
* **Monitor moves:** Track the status and progress of ongoing moves across OneDrive, SharePoint sites, and Microsoft 365 Groups.

The SharePoint admin sees the Multi-Geo skill in action.

#### Catalog skill – General Availability

The Catalog skill connects the SharePoint Admin Agent to Catalog Management, so the agent understands your tenant the way your business is organized. Using built-in categories like Department and Locale, along with any custom categories you've added, the agent can:

* **Show how content is organized in your tenant:** View site counts, site lists and groups of content in Catalog.
* **Organize content using the skill:** Leverage Catalog skill to create most relevant groups of SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts with recommendations such as group sites in a certain department that are Highly Confidential.
* **Recommend next steps:** such as inactive content cleanup, archiving, version-history limits or a permissions review, scoped to the right group of sites instead of the whole tenant.

The SharePoint admin sees the catalog management skill in action.

#### Governance Hub for Admins – Generally Available Dec. 2026

As organizations accelerate their AI transformation, content governance can quickly become overwhelming. Admins don’t need more reports. They need to know what needs attention, what to do next, and have a simple way to act.

Today, we’re thrilled to introduce **Governance Hub** for Admins, **powered by the SharePoint Admin Agent** . It is readily available in Home tab of the SharePoint Admin Center and brings assessments, findings, recommendations, and actionable tasks together into a single experience - helping admins move from insight to action and govern content at scale

The SharePoint Admin Agent helps govern content from a single experience.

#### 2\. Agent governance in the lens of Microsoft 365 resources SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams

SharePoint and Teams administrators often ask – for my top secret and confidential resources, which agents are accessing them and who instantiated them, can I control at site or team level which agents are allowed? We have an answer for you.

Agent 365 offers a breadth view of all agents in your enterprise. To complement that breadth view, we are introducing depth view of agents in the lens of Microsoft 365 resources, specifically SharePoint sites, Teams, and OneDrive under the umbrella of Agent Lineage.

The new **Agent governance** node in the SharePoint admin center puts every agent governance action against Microsoft 365 resources in one place. Admins can go from insight to action without switching between reports and settings.

Govern how agents are interacting with content.

# Build once, reuse across your agent fleet: Tools and Toolboxes in Foundry

[Linda](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/author/zhuoqunli) ,

[Nandini](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/author/nandinim)

Connecting one tool to one agent is not hard. The challenge is managing a useful set of tools and agentic capabilities across a fleet of production agents at scale. Every new agent shouldn’t require you to build the same integrations, copy the same instructions, and troubleshoot the same dependencies. And adding a useful capability shouldn’t require a separate rollout in every agent application.

[Toolboxes](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/toolbox-overview) in Microsoft Foundry turn tools, [skills](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/skills) , and agents into shared capabilities. Curate and version them in Foundry, expose them through one MCP endpoint, and reuse them across Foundry agents and other MCP-compatible frameworks and runtimes. Toolbox centralizes downstream authentication, so each agent connects to the toolbox instead of managing credentials for every tool. [Tool search in Toolbox](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/tool-search) lets agents discover the tools they need on demand, so the shared catalog can grow without filling the context window with every tool definition.

At Ignite, we are excited to launch the following enhancements:

* **Skills support expanded:** Manage skills with the Skills CRUD API (GA, coming soon), and execute skills in prompt agent via [Shell tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/skills-shell-tool) (preview). Toolbox will also expose skills through the official [MCP Skills extension](https://skills.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/) for use across compatible agents and frameworks.
* [**Web Search**](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/web-search) **powered by** [**Web IQ**](https://learn.microsoft.com/web-iq/resources/faq) **:** available in prompt agent and coming soon in Toolbox, with AI-native retrieval optimized for grounding quality, speed, and token efficiency.
* [**Fabric IQ**](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/fabric-iq) **enhancement(preview):** Discover 60+ Fabric item types, with latency and tracing improvements for semantic model and data agent integration.
* [**Work IQ**](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/quickstart/foundry) **enhancement** **(** **preview** **):** The Work IQ API brings together Web IQ and Foundry IQ at Ignite, with Fabric IQ integration to follow.
* [**A2A tool and endpoints**](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/agent-to-agent) **:** Orchestrate Foundry and external agents with the generally available A2A tool. A2A endpoints are generally available on prompt agents and in public preview on hosted agents (coming soon).
* **New catalog partners:** Bring Snowflake, MongoDB and Databricks into your agents, from governed analytics to application data.
* [**Toolboxes in GitHub Copilot**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/use-toolbox-vs-code) **:** Install a toolbox in VS Code with one-click setup, sign in with your Microsoft Entra account, and discover and call its tools from Copilot.
* [**Toolbox** **monitor d** **ashboard**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/monitor-toolbox) **:** See adoption, success rates, errors, and consumption across agents using the same toolbox.
* [**Tool policy**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/control-plane/govern-tools) **(preview):** Use Azure Policy and project configurations to enforce approved-tool configurations across Foundry agents and toolboxes.
* [**Browser automation**](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/browser-automation) **(Generally Available):** Let agents interact with web apps in secure, isolated browser sessions, with full observability, proxies and private network access, human -in the loop and secret management, Captcha and Web Bot Auth handling—all through one tool.
* **[Computer Use](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/computer-use?pivots=python) (Generally Available):** Use the latest OpenAI computer use enabled models (Astra series) and specific tool actions on your target application.

## Customer Story

_“The real value of AI agents comes from giving them the right tools and skills to act on the information around them. In our systems, we have worked with Microsoft to bring Toolboxes and Skills together with our operational data and business systems, enabling our agents to find information, generate insights and support our teams more effectively across daily operations.”_ From Ahmed AbdulJalil Ebrahim, Manager Digital Innovation & Process Management, Gulf Air

## Build: give agents the context, expertise, and execution they need

A useful toolbox gives agents the capabilities to find information, apply expertise, and take action. Combine Web Search powered by Web IQ for current web information, skills for task-specific expertise, Fabric IQ for business data and semantics, and Work IQ for organizational context through the unified Microsoft IQ endpoint.

### Skills support expanded

Give agents the expertise to do specialized work, from analyzing business data to preparing customer briefings and reviewing documents against company standards. [Skills](https://agentskills.io/) capture the knowledge, guidance, and examples agents need for those tasks, so teams do not have to teach every agent from scratch. The Skills CRUD API general availability is coming soon, making it easier to create, manage, and version skills as business needs evolve.

A prompt agent can use a skill to analyze a spreadsheet, calculate trends, and produce a report in the team’s format. This support is now in public preview through the [Shell tool in Toolbox](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/skills-shell-tool?view=foundry&tabs=python) . Shell provides the managed environment to load skills and execute required code, so developers can focus on the result instead of setting up execution infrastructure.

Toolbox will make that expertise easier to share through the official [MCP Skills extension](https://skills.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/) . Hosted agent in Foundry and other compatible agents and frameworks will be able to find and use skills alongside the tools that support them.

[Creating an ops-analysis skill, inspecting its instructions, and adding it to a toolbox.](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-skills.gif)

### Web Search: better grounding, powered by Web IQ

General Web Search is now powered by Web IQ, bringing AI-native web grounding to both prompt agent and coming soon in Toolboxes. Web IQ prioritizes relevant, fresh, and authoritative information and returns focused, citation-ready context, helping agents ground their answers in useful evidence and show where it came from.

That gives agents a stronger foundation for work that depends on what is happening now: checking a new service advisory, researching a market shift, or gathering the most up-to-date evidence for a recommendation. Faster retrieval keeps multi-step research moving, while focused results use context more efficiently and leave more room for the agent to reason.

Add Web Search directly to a Foundry agent or share it through a toolbox, with no separate Web IQ connection setup. For searches restricted to specific domains, the existing [Grounding with Bing Custom Search](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/web-search) option continues to apply.

[Configuring Web Search powered by Web IQ for a shared toolbox.](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-web-search.gif)

### Fabric IQ: turn business context into better agent decisions

Finding the right business context shouldn’t be a separate integration project for every agent. Fabric IQ models how your business operates, and the Fabric IQ tool in Foundry connects your agents to that context through Power BI semantic models, ontologies, and Fabric data agents. Now in preview, the tool can discover more than 60 Fabric item types, so developers can see what’s already available across their organization. Browse and filter that catalog, then connect the semantic models, ontologies, or data agents your workflow needs.

This helps agents move from “What happened?” to “What does it mean for the business?” An operations agent could identify which processes and customer segments are affected by a spike in checkout failures, using the metric definitions and access permissions already set in Fabric. The business meaning travels with the data instead of being recreated in each agent’s instructions.

We’re also making existing Power BI semantic model and Fabric data agent integrations faster and easier to debug. Lower latency and clearer query-based tracing help you test and troubleshoot an agent before it goes to production, and end-to-end tracing lets you monitor it once it’s live.

[fabric iq catalog high res 20261118 unblurred image](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/fabric-iq-catalog-high-res-20261118-unblurred.gif)

### Work IQ: bring Microsoft IQ into your agent workflows

At Ignite, the Work IQ API provides access to Web IQ and Foundry IQ, available in preview, with Fabric IQ coming next. Developers connect once, then combine organizational and external web context with their own tools, skills, and specialist agents in Foundry. That reduces the separate integrations each agent needs and makes organizational context part of the shared capability set.

Microsoft IQ gives agents more than access to data: it gives them the context to understand the business and what’s currently happening in the world. Through Work IQ, agents can connect knowledge across Microsoft 365 with business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Apps. Semantic understanding and agent-ready context help them produce grounded answers, reason across sources, and take action without developers having to assemble separate retrieval pipelines. That intelligence is permission-aware, so agents work within what each user is allowed to see and do.

### A2A: connect agents to work together

Solve complex tasks with a team of specialist agents, not a single agent that has to do everything. The A2A tool and A2A endpoints in Foundry Agent Service use the stable 1.0 version of [A2A protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) . A2A endpoints are generally available on prompt agents and public preview on hosted agents coming soon. Expose an agent’s expertise for others to use, or have a Foundry agent delegate work to a Foundry or external A2A-compatible agent. Developers can orchestrate across agents without copying every agent’s instructions and integrations into one large agent.

In an incident workflow, an on-call agent can gather operational evidence, ask an agent to assess business impact, and bring the results into one recommendation. An incident-review agent can call that same agent for its analysis. Each team keeps ownership of its domain expertise and release cycle while making that expertise available to other agents. The coordinator defines the task, supplies the context, and decides the next action; Toolbox makes the connected agent reusable across authorized callers.

[Inspecting the A2A connection experience for a specialist agent.](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-a2a.gif)

### New partners: bring Snowflake, MongoDB, and Databricks into your agents

At Ignite, we’re welcoming new partners to the Foundry tools catalog, including [Snowflake](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp) , [MongoDB](https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongodb-mcp-server) , and [Databricks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/agents/mcp-tools/genie-agent) . Bring agents closer to the data and systems your teams already use, without making every integration a project of its own.

An analytics agent can use Snowflake’s governed search, business definitions, and data agents to answer business questions. A developer assistant can explore MongoDB collections and query application data while investigating an issue. The catalog gives teams a common place to discover these capabilities, review each partner’s setup and authentication requirements, and choose the integrations that fit their agents.

_“Business intent lives in Microsoft 365, and for many customers, enterprise data lives in Azure Databricks. Genie One in Microsoft Foundry brings governed Databricks intelligence to the agents customers build in Foundry, with the same permissions and business definitions they already trust.”_ From David Meyer, SVP Products, Databricks

_“Enterprises want to build AI agents where their teams already work, without giving up control of their most valuable data. With the Snowflake MCP Server in Microsoft Foundry, developers can bring Snowflake Cortex Agents and governed enterprise data into the agents they build, with every request governed by the Snowflake permissions customers already rely on. It gives our joint customers the choice to build on their platform of choice and the trust to turn insights into outcomes.”_ From Pavan Pothukuchi, Head of AI Platform, Snowflake

_“AI agents are only as useful as the data and context they can access. By connecting MongoDB Atlas with Microsoft Foundry, we’re making it easier for developers to build intelligent agents grounded in real-time operational data. This is an important step toward bringing MongoDB’s operational data directly into the AI workflows developers are building with Microsoft._ _”_ From Ben Cefalo, Chief Product Officer, MongoDB

## Consume: bring your toolbox into GitHub Copilot

As enterprises empower their developers to achieve more with coding agent, toolboxes provide a central hub to curate, consume and manage their agentic capabilities. Toolboxes now offer [one-click setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/use-toolbox-vs-code) in GitHub Copilot in VS Code. Start on the Toolboxes tab in Foundry and choose Install in VS Code. Confirm the installation in VS Code to add the toolbox’s MCP endpoint without copying URLs or editing configuration files.

When authentication is needed, VS Code prompts users to sign in with the Microsoft Entra account they use for Foundry. Copilot connects to the toolbox as that user, preserving their identity rather than relying on a shared toolbox credential. Each underlying tool continues to use its [configured authentication and access controls](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/tool-authentication) .

Developers can then ask Copilot to find relevant documentation, investigate an issue, or work with an approved data source. With Tool Search enabled, Copilot discovers the capabilities needed for the task and calls the selected tools on demand. Developers can inspect those searches and tool calls in chat, while platform teams maintain the shared capability set in Foundry.

[Installing a toolbox from Foundry into VS Code, connecting with a user's Entra account, and calling Web Search from GitHub Copilot.](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-consume-unmasked.gif)

## Manage: operate shared capabilities with visibility and control

Sharing capabilities should make production easier to operate, not just development faster. Toolbox monitor dashboard and tool policy give platform teams foundations for reuse at scale: visibility into how capabilities perform and clear rules for what developers can configure.

### Monitor dashboard: see what is used, find what needs attention

Shared tools are production dependencies. When multiple agents rely on the same toolbox, an issue in one tool can affect several workflows. Platform teams need a shared view of adoption and reliability to scale reuse without losing sight of what their agents depend on.

For platform owners, that means knowing where to invest, which issues deserve attention, and what drives consumption. For agent developers, it means understanding how the shared tools their application uses are behaving. A common operational view helps both teams prioritize improvements and investigate problems without each team having to assemble its own reporting.

Toolbox monitor dashboard provides that view with call volume, success rates, error trends, active agents, tool selection, skill and A2A usage, and a consumption breakdown. Filter by toolbox version, time range, and agent to see how usage and reliability vary across consumers. Use the dashboard to identify where to focus, then inspect the consuming agent’s traces when you need the details of an individual call.

[ignite26 foundry monitor unmasked image](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-monitor-unmasked.gif)

### Tool policy: give developers a clear path to approved capabilities

As an agent fleet grows, reviewing every integration manually slows teams down, while duplicating governance checks in each application makes them harder to keep consistent. Tool policy lets platform teams define the rules centrally and apply them as agents and toolboxes evolve.

[Tool governance with Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/control-plane/govern-tools) , in public preview, provides an approved-tools policy for Foundry agents and toolboxes. Administrators specify allowed tool types, MCP endpoints, and MCP connectors. Developers get clear boundaries for choosing capabilities, and platform owners can apply the same configuration requirements across teams.

The policy evaluates configurations when agents and toolboxes are created or updated and when tools are invoked through agents or toolboxes. Start with the Audit effect to identify noncompliant configurations without blocking saves, then use Deny to reject configurations outside the approved set.

[ignite26 foundry tool policy unmasked image](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-tool-policy-unmasked.gif)

## Browser Automation: Secure isolated browsers for enterprise agents

Much of the work that keeps a business running still happens in a browser: internal portals, vendor consoles and legacy apps with no API. The **Browser automation tool in Foundry Agent Service powered by Azure Playwright Workspaces** is generally available and gives every Foundry agent a managed browser with the below capabilities.

The Browser automation tool expands the agent builder with MCP tool primitives and action batching, code execution for more efficient and performant agents, plus human-in-the-loop takeover to steer agents through authentication, site glitches. Observability via session recordings is generally available, while private website access through VNet injection is in preview.

At Ignite, additional capabilities in preview are enabled with Browser automation tool – bring your own browser proxy, secret management via Azure Key Vault so that model does not see the secrets, Captcha & Web bot Auth management and state management with profile reuse (coming soon), for your agentic automation workloads.

[Processing invoices across a browser application and Excel with the Browser Automation tool.](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-browser-automation-animated.gif) Web Bot Auth ( [based on IETF draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-meunier-web-bot-auth-architecture) ) enables AI agents to cryptographically sign their HTTP requests which can help in verifying the agent’s identity for public website research tasks. We are enabling Web Bot Auth for customers through two methods: Customer self-registration OR Microsoft platform registration (via selected bot management providers like **Akamai, Cloudflare, and F5** ). [Complete this form](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/feSSnFeQMq "https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/fessnfeqmq") to express interest in Microsoft platform registration.
Browser automation tool works across agent types – prompt, copilot harness or hosted agents. Learn more [here](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/?p=3334&preview=true) .

## Computer Use: Explore full power of CUA models with this tool

When the automation scenarios need both desktop and browser automation then developers can lean on to **Computer Use Tool in Foundry Agent Service** . Happy to announce that [Computer use tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/computer-use?pivots=python) is generally available with OpenAI’s computer use supported models where customers bring their own harness and target application and utilize the specific actions to complete computer use related tasks.

## Get started: build a shared troubleshooting toolbox

Create a versioned analysis skill, combine it with public documentation and Web Search, and expose the set through one MCP endpoint.

Use a model deployment that supports the Shell tool. The sample mounts the skill in a managed Shell container for the prompt agent and also exposes it to compatible MCP Skills clients.

### 1\. Create the skill and toolbox

```
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from azure.ai.projects.models import (
    MCPToolboxTool,
    ShellToolboxTool,
    SkillInlineContent,
    SkillReferenceParam,
    ToolboxShellContainerAutoEnvironment,
    ToolboxSkillReference,
    ToolSearchToolboxTool,
    WebSearchToolboxTool,
)
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

endpoint = "https://<account>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>"

with (
    AIProjectClient(
        endpoint=endpoint, credential=DefaultAzureCredential(), allow_preview=True,
    ) as project,
):
    skill = project.beta.skills.create(
        name="ops-analysis",
        inline_content=SkillInlineContent(
            description="Investigate an operational issue and recommend next steps.",
            instructions="""# Ops analysis
- Gather metrics, incident details, and deployment history when available.
- Compare equivalent time windows and show the calculations.
- Separate observed facts, hypotheses, and missing evidence.
- Use public documentation to support troubleshooting recommendations.
- Cite the source of each factual claim.
- If operational data is unavailable, ask for it. Do not invent it.
- Recommend a next action; do not change a service without explicit approval.
""",
        ),
    )
    version = project.toolboxes.create_version(
        name="ops-analysis-starter",
        description="Public troubleshooting references and shared ops guidance.",
        tools=[
            MCPToolboxTool(
                server_label="mslearn",
                server_url="https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp",
                require_approval="never",
            ),
            WebSearchToolboxTool(name="public_web"),
            ShellToolboxTool(
                name="ops-analysis-shell",
                environment=ToolboxShellContainerAutoEnvironment(
                    skills=[
                        SkillReferenceParam(
                            skill_id=skill.skill_id, version=skill.version
                        )
                    ],
                ),
            ),
            ToolSearchToolboxTool(),
        ],
        skills=[ToolboxSkillReference(name=skill.name, version=skill.version)],
    )
    print(f"Skill version: {skill.version}")
    print(f"Toolbox version: {version.version}")
    print(
        f"{endpoint}/toolboxes/{version.name}"
        f"/versions/{version.version}/mcp?api-version=v1"
    )
```

### 2\. Use the toolbox in a prompt agent

Set the project endpoint, your model deployment name, and the toolbox endpoint printed in step 1.

```
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from azure.ai.projects.models import MCPTool, PromptAgentDefinition
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

endpoint = "https://<account>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>"
model_deployment = "<model-deployment-name>"
toolbox_endpoint = "<version-specific MCP endpoint printed above>"

with (
    AIProjectClient(
        endpoint=endpoint, credential=DefaultAzureCredential(), allow_preview=True,
    ) as project,
):
    agent = project.agents.create_version(
        agent_name="ops-troubleshooter",
        definition=PromptAgentDefinition(
            model=model_deployment,
            instructions=(
                "Use the toolbox's Shell tool to read and follow the ops-analysis skill. "
                "Use the toolbox's search tools for documentation. "
                "Cite sources; ask for missing data."
            ),
            tools=[
                MCPTool(
                    server_label="ops_toolbox",
                    server_url=toolbox_endpoint,
                    require_approval="never",
                )
            ],
        ),
    )
    with project.get_openai_client(agent_name=agent.name) as openai:
        response = openai.responses.create(
            input=(
                "Use the ops-analysis skill to find Microsoft Learn guidance for high latency "
                "in Azure App Service. Summarize three checks and cite sources."
            )
        )
        if response.status != "completed":
            raise RuntimeError(response.model_dump_json())
        print(response.output_text)
```

# Build once, reuse across your agent fleet: Tools and Toolboxes in Foundry

[Linda](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/author/zhuoqunli) ,

[Nandini](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/author/nandinim)

Connecting one tool to one agent is not hard. The challenge is managing a useful set of tools and agentic capabilities across a fleet of production agents at scale. Every new agent shouldn’t require you to build the same integrations, copy the same instructions, and troubleshoot the same dependencies. And adding a useful capability shouldn’t require a separate rollout in every agent application.

[Toolboxes](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/toolbox-overview) in Microsoft Foundry turn tools, [skills](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/skills) , and agents into shared capabilities. Curate and version them in Foundry, expose them through one MCP endpoint, and reuse them across Foundry agents and other MCP-compatible frameworks and runtimes. Toolbox centralizes downstream authentication, so each agent connects to the toolbox instead of managing credentials for every tool. [Tool search in Toolbox](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/tool-search) lets agents discover the tools they need on demand, so the shared catalog can grow without filling the context window with every tool definition.

At Ignite, we are excited to launch the following enhancements:

* **Skills support expanded:** Manage skills with the Skills CRUD API (GA, coming soon), and execute skills in prompt agent via [Shell tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/skills-shell-tool) (preview). Toolbox will also expose skills through the official [MCP Skills extension](https://skills.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/) for use across compatible agents and frameworks.
* [**Web Search**](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/web-search) **powered by** [**Web IQ**](https://learn.microsoft.com/web-iq/resources/faq) **:** available in prompt agent and coming soon in Toolbox, with AI-native retrieval optimized for grounding quality, speed, and token efficiency.
* [**Fabric IQ**](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/fabric-iq) **enhancement(preview):** Discover 60+ Fabric item types, with latency and tracing improvements for semantic model and data agent integration.
* [**Work IQ**](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/quickstart/foundry) **enhancement** **(** **preview** **):** The Work IQ API brings together Web IQ and Foundry IQ at Ignite, with Fabric IQ integration to follow.
* [**A2A tool and endpoints**](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/agent-to-agent) **:** Orchestrate Foundry and external agents with the generally available A2A tool. A2A endpoints are generally available on prompt agents and in public preview on hosted agents (coming soon).
* **New catalog partners:** Bring Snowflake, MongoDB and Databricks into your agents, from governed analytics to application data.
* [**Toolboxes in GitHub Copilot**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/use-toolbox-vs-code) **:** Install a toolbox in VS Code with one-click setup, sign in with your Microsoft Entra account, and discover and call its tools from Copilot.
* [**Toolbox** **monitor d** **ashboard**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/monitor-toolbox) **:** See adoption, success rates, errors, and consumption across agents using the same toolbox.
* [**Tool policy**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/control-plane/govern-tools) **(preview):** Use Azure Policy and project configurations to enforce approved-tool configurations across Foundry agents and toolboxes.
* [**Browser automation**](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/browser-automation) **(Generally Available):** Let agents interact with web apps in secure, isolated browser sessions, with full observability, proxies and private network access, human -in the loop and secret management, Captcha and Web Bot Auth handling—all through one tool.
* **[Computer Use](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/computer-use?pivots=python) (Generally Available):** Use the latest OpenAI computer use enabled models (Astra series) and specific tool actions on your target application.

## Customer Story

_“The real value of AI agents comes from giving them the right tools and skills to act on the information around them. In our systems, we have worked with Microsoft to bring Toolboxes and Skills together with our operational data and business systems, enabling our agents to find information, generate insights and support our teams more effectively across daily operations.”_ From Ahmed AbdulJalil Ebrahim, Manager Digital Innovation & Process Management, Gulf Air

## Build: give agents the context, expertise, and execution they need

A useful toolbox gives agents the capabilities to find information, apply expertise, and take action. Combine Web Search powered by Web IQ for current web information, skills for task-specific expertise, Fabric IQ for business data and semantics, and Work IQ for organizational context through the unified Microsoft IQ endpoint.

### Skills support expanded

Give agents the expertise to do specialized work, from analyzing business data to preparing customer briefings and reviewing documents against company standards. [Skills](https://agentskills.io/) capture the knowledge, guidance, and examples agents need for those tasks, so teams do not have to teach every agent from scratch. The Skills CRUD API general availability is coming soon, making it easier to create, manage, and version skills as business needs evolve.

A prompt agent can use a skill to analyze a spreadsheet, calculate trends, and produce a report in the team’s format. This support is now in public preview through the [Shell tool in Toolbox](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/skills-shell-tool?view=foundry&tabs=python) . Shell provides the managed environment to load skills and execute required code, so developers can focus on the result instead of setting up execution infrastructure.

Toolbox will make that expertise easier to share through the official [MCP Skills extension](https://skills.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/) . Hosted agent in Foundry and other compatible agents and frameworks will be able to find and use skills alongside the tools that support them.

[Creating an ops-analysis skill, inspecting its instructions, and adding it to a toolbox.](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-skills.gif)

### Web Search: better grounding, powered by Web IQ

General Web Search is now powered by Web IQ, bringing AI-native web grounding to both prompt agent and coming soon in Toolboxes. Web IQ prioritizes relevant, fresh, and authoritative information and returns focused, citation-ready context, helping agents ground their answers in useful evidence and show where it came from.

That gives agents a stronger foundation for work that depends on what is happening now: checking a new service advisory, researching a market shift, or gathering the most up-to-date evidence for a recommendation. Faster retrieval keeps multi-step research moving, while focused results use context more efficiently and leave more room for the agent to reason.

Add Web Search directly to a Foundry agent or share it through a toolbox, with no separate Web IQ connection setup. For searches restricted to specific domains, the existing [Grounding with Bing Custom Search](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/web-search) option continues to apply.

[Configuring Web Search powered by Web IQ for a shared toolbox.](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-web-search.gif)

### Fabric IQ: turn business context into better agent decisions

Finding the right business context shouldn’t be a separate integration project for every agent. Fabric IQ models how your business operates, and the Fabric IQ tool in Foundry connects your agents to that context through Power BI semantic models, ontologies, and Fabric data agents. Now in preview, the tool can discover more than 60 Fabric item types, so developers can see what’s already available across their organization. Browse and filter that catalog, then connect the semantic models, ontologies, or data agents your workflow needs.

This helps agents move from “What happened?” to “What does it mean for the business?” An operations agent could identify which processes and customer segments are affected by a spike in checkout failures, using the metric definitions and access permissions already set in Fabric. The business meaning travels with the data instead of being recreated in each agent’s instructions.

We’re also making existing Power BI semantic model and Fabric data agent integrations faster and easier to debug. Lower latency and clearer query-based tracing help you test and troubleshoot an agent before it goes to production, and end-to-end tracing lets you monitor it once it’s live.

[fabric iq catalog high res 20261118 unblurred image](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/fabric-iq-catalog-high-res-20261118-unblurred.gif)

### Work IQ: bring Microsoft IQ into your agent workflows

At Ignite, the Work IQ API provides access to Web IQ and Foundry IQ, available in preview, with Fabric IQ coming next. Developers connect once, then combine organizational and external web context with their own tools, skills, and specialist agents in Foundry. That reduces the separate integrations each agent needs and makes organizational context part of the shared capability set.

Microsoft IQ gives agents more than access to data: it gives them the context to understand the business and what’s currently happening in the world. Through Work IQ, agents can connect knowledge across Microsoft 365 with business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Apps. Semantic understanding and agent-ready context help them produce grounded answers, reason across sources, and take action without developers having to assemble separate retrieval pipelines. That intelligence is permission-aware, so agents work within what each user is allowed to see and do.

### A2A: connect agents to work together

Solve complex tasks with a team of specialist agents, not a single agent that has to do everything. The A2A tool and A2A endpoints in Foundry Agent Service use the stable 1.0 version of [A2A protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) . A2A endpoints are generally available on prompt agents and public preview on hosted agents coming soon. Expose an agent’s expertise for others to use, or have a Foundry agent delegate work to a Foundry or external A2A-compatible agent. Developers can orchestrate across agents without copying every agent’s instructions and integrations into one large agent.

In an incident workflow, an on-call agent can gather operational evidence, ask an agent to assess business impact, and bring the results into one recommendation. An incident-review agent can call that same agent for its analysis. Each team keeps ownership of its domain expertise and release cycle while making that expertise available to other agents. The coordinator defines the task, supplies the context, and decides the next action; Toolbox makes the connected agent reusable across authorized callers.

[Inspecting the A2A connection experience for a specialist agent.](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2026/11/ignite26-foundry-a2a.gif)

### New partners: bring Snowflake, MongoDB, and Databricks into your agents

At Ignite, we’re welcoming new partners to the Foundry tools catalog, including [Snowflake](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp) , [MongoDB](https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongodb-mcp-server) , and [Databricks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/agents/mcp-tools/genie-agent) . Bring agents closer to the data and systems your teams already use, without making every integration a project of its own.

An analytics agent can use Snowflake’s governed search, business definitions, and data agents to answer business questions. A developer assistant can explore MongoDB collections and query application data while investigating an issue. The catalog gives teams a common place to discover these capabilities, review each partner’s setup and authentication requirements, and choose the integrations that fit their agents.

_“Business intent lives in Microsoft 365, and for many customers, enterprise data lives in Azure Databricks. Genie One in Microsoft Foundry brings governed Databricks intelligence to the agents customers build in Foundry, with the same permissions and business definitions they already trust.”_ From David Meyer, SVP Products, Databricks

_“Enterprises want to build AI agents where their teams already work, without giving up control of their most valuable data. With the Snowflake MCP Server in Microsoft Foundry, developers can bring Snowflake Cortex Agents and governed enterprise data into the agents they build, with every request governed by the Snowflake permissions customers already rely on. It gives our joint customers the choice to build on their platform of choice and the trust to turn insights into outcomes.”_ From Pavan Pothukuchi, Head of AI Platform, Snowflake

_“AI agents are only as useful as the data and context they can access. By connecting MongoDB Atlas with Microsoft Foundry, we’re making it easier for developers to build intelligent agents grounded in real-time operational data. This is an important step toward bringing MongoDB’s operational data directly into the AI workflows developers are building with Microsoft._ _”_ From Ben Cefalo, Chief Product Officer, MongoDB

## Consume: bring your toolbox into GitHub Copilot

As enterprises empower their developers to achieve more with coding agent, toolboxes provide a central hub to curate, consume and manage their agentic capabilities. Toolboxes now offer [one-click setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/use-toolbox-vs-code) in GitHub Copilot in VS Code. Start on the Toolboxes tab in Foundry and choose Install in VS Code. Confirm the installation in VS Code to add the toolbox’s MCP endpoint without copying URLs or editing configuration files.

When authentication is needed, VS Code prompts users to sign in with the Microsoft Entra account they use

# What’s new in Azure Managed Redis at Microsoft Ignite 2026

[Ibukun_Martins's avatar](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/users/ibukun_martins/3597014)

[Ibukun\_Martins](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/users/ibukun_martins/3597014)

Nov 17, 2026

We’re excited to share what’s new in [Azure Managed Redis](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/managed-redis/) at [Microsoft Ignite 2026](https://ignite.microsoft.com/en-US/home) . As enterprises build AI-powered applications and scale the ones they already rely on, we’re continuing to invest in capabilities that help them grow with confidence.

Today, we’re announcing seven updates to Azure Managed Redis to help you build AI-powered applications, simplify migration, and manage production workloads. The public previews of Redis 8 and the Azure Managed Redis agent kit lead these announcements, alongside updates for database caching, shard-level monitoring, network access, and event-driven applications. Here’s what’s new and where to get started.

**1\. Build modern and AI-powered applications with Redis 8 (Public preview)**

Build semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), recommendations, and agent memory with new vector capabilities in Redis 8. Richer queries, atomic JSON updates, field-level expiration, and fine-grained security give developers additional ways to work with application and AI data.

For applications that combine structured data with vector search, these capabilities expand what you can query and manage within Azure Managed Redis.

Learn more about Redis 8: <https://aka.ms/amr-redis8>

**2\. Apply Redis best practices with Azure Managed Redis agent kit (Public preview)**

Bring Redis and Azure best-practice guidance into your AI-assisted development workflow. The Azure Managed Redis agent kit provides recommendations for client configuration, resilience, performance, and Azure deployment, alongside guided migration workflows.

For example, use the guidance to review client configuration and resilience choices as you prepare an application for production. The kit supports development and operational decisions; it is not an agent runtime.

Explore the agent kit announcement: <https://aka.ms/amr-agent-kit>

#### **Simplify migration and database caching**

**3\. Azure Cache for Redis to Azure Managed Redis Migration Tooling (General availability)**

Built-in DNS migration tooling helps reduce application configuration changes when moving from Azure Cache for Redis to Azure Managed Redis. Redirect an existing cache hostname to an Azure Managed Redis instance, with optional data retention to support migration.

For teams managing existing applications, hostname redirection simplifies one part of the cutover: changing where applications connect while retaining the hostname they already use.

Learn more about this announcement: <https://aka.ms/amrmigrationtooling>

**4\. Implement database caching patterns with integration guidance (General availability)**

Choosing what to cache is as important as adding a cache. Database integration guidance provides caching patterns, reference architectures, and tutorials for applications using Azure SQL Database, Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure Database for PostgreSQL.

Start with frequently requested database data, then use the guidance to evaluate a caching approach that can reduce repeated database requests and improve application responsiveness.  Each guide has a fully deployable sample app to help you get started adding Azure Managed Redis into your database-backed apps.

Explore database caching guidance: <https://aka.ms/amr-database-integrations>

#### **Operate with greater visibility and control**

**5\. Investigate workload imbalances with shard-level metrics in Azure Managed Redis (Public preview)**

Inspect memory usage, key counts, and replication health for individual shards using Azure Monitor telemetry.

When investigating performance, use this added detail to understand whether workloads are distributed unevenly across shards and identify potential hotspots for further investigation.

Explore the shard-level metrics update: <https://aka.ms/redis/whatsnew>

**6\. Control endpoint access with IP filtering in Azure Managed Redis (Public preview)**

Control access to publicly accessible cache endpoints with firewall rules. Restrict connections to approved source IP addresses or Azure service tags.

For example, use approved application source IP addresses to narrow which clients can reach a public cache endpoint.

Explore the IP filtering update: <https://aka.ms/redis/whatsnew>

**7\. Respond to cache changes with Azure Managed Redis keyspace notifications (General availability)**

Subscribe to Redis Pub/Sub notifications for key updates, deletions, and expirations. Applications can respond to relevant cache events without continuously polling for changes.

For example, an application can subscribe to expiration events and use those notifications to trigger downstream logic.

Explore keyspace notification configuration: <https://aka.ms/amr-keyspace-notifications>

**Take the next step with Azure Managed Redis**

Build your next AI-powered application, bring caching to an existing app, or move forward with your migration. Explore what’s new, choose where to start, and put Azure Managed Redis to work.

[Start building today](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/redis/quickstart-create-managed-redis) with the step-by-step guide to creating your first instance.

[Explore tutorials and documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/redis/) to connect Redis to your applications.

[Find the right pricing option](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/managed-redis/) for your workload.

[Keep up with the latest updates](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/category/azuredatabases/blog/azure-managed-redis) through product announcements, technical guidance, and examples.

Language should not stand between people. Live Interpreter API , our real-time speech-to-speech translation service, now runs on a new LLM-based model that translates speech while people are still talking.

* **Breakthrough translation quality** **:** 30% fewer translation errors than the previous production model.
